question: Which uses the most energy: a full phone charge, an evening of LED light, boiling a litre, a hot shower or a 10 km drive?
answer: The drive, then the shower. Heating water and moving a tonne of car take energy on a scale chargers never reach: about 5 kWh for 10 km in a petrol car, about 2 for an 8-minute shower, 0.02 for a full phone charge. Unplugging chargers is tidy; a shorter shower shows on the bill.
move: Energy goes where things are heated or moved; look there first.
source: Arithmetic from heat capacity and fuel energy
reference: Water: 4.18 kJ per kg per degree; petrol: about 32 MJ (8.9 kWh) per litre; assumptions: 6 L per 100 km, a 4,000 mAh 3.85 V phone battery with charger losses, a 10 W LED for 5 hours, 8 L a minute of shower water warmed by 25 degrees
ask: Which of my daily habits heats water or moves a heavy machine?

items.label: Full phone charge
items.note: A year of daily charges, about 7 kWh, matches a single 14 km drive.

items.label: 8-minute hot shower
items.note: 64 litres warmed by 25 °C: as much as about 90 phone charges.

items.label: LED bulb, 5 hours
items.note: A 10-watt bulb for a whole evening.

items.label: Drive 10 km
items.note: 0.6 litres of petrol: over 250 phone charges' worth.

items.label: Boil 1 litre
items.note: Water is slow to heat: one litre to boiling takes about 0.1 kWh.
